title: 3rd Truth The Importance Of This Mystery And Reference To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What is the main subject of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains a deep truth about Allah’s oneness and power, especially that for Allah, creating the greatest thing and the smallest thing are equally easy.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is this truth very important in Islam?
questions.answer: It is described as one of the strongest foundations of Islam and one of the deepest sources of faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say this truth helps open and explain?
questions.answer: It helps uncover the deep meanings of the Qur’an and the hidden mystery in the creation of beings.

questions.question: How is philosophy described when facing this mystery?
questions.answer: It is shown as unable to fully solve or overpower it.

questions.question: To whom is repeated thanks and praise given in the passage?
questions.answer: To the Merciful Creator.

questions.question: What work is said to have explained and proven this mystery?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say those proofs are?
questions.answer: It says they are as certain and clear as a basic math fact.

questions.question: Does the passage try to explain the whole matter in full detail here, or something less?
questions.answer: It only plans to give a short outline of the main foundations and proofs.

questions.question: How many mysteries does the passage say it intends to point to?
questions.answer: Thirteen.

questions.question: How are those thirteen mysteries compared to help the reader understand them?
questions.answer: They are compared to steps or to a table of contents.

questions.question: Which of those mysteries had already been written?
questions.answer: The first and second.

questions.question: Why was the rest not completed?
questions.answer: Two strong obstacles, one material and one immaterial, caused the writer to stop.

questions.question: What question or problem is this passage mainly trying to address?
questions.answer: It is trying to explain and prove the mystery of Divine unity, especially how all things are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: What comparison is used to describe Allah’s creating the largest and smallest things?
questions.answer: The passage says there is no real difference for Allah between creating something huge and something tiny.

questions.question: What effect does understanding this truth have on a person’s view of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It helps a person see the Qur’an’s deep meanings more clearly.

questions.question: What kind of hidden matter in creation does the passage say becomes knowable through this explanation?
questions.answer: A very secret mystery about how beings are created becomes better understood.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this mystery is beyond ordinary human thinking?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a very deep riddle that human reason by itself cannot fully reach.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage express after saying this mystery was solved?
questions.answer: Strong gratitude and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What role does the Risale-i Nur have in the passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as the work that solved, uncovered, and established this truth with strong proof.

questions.question: Does the passage say the proof is weak, probable, or decisive?
questions.answer: It says the proof is decisive and certain.

questions.question: What does the passage decide to do instead of repeating all the long proofs?
questions.answer: It leaves the full explanation to other parts of the Risale-i Nur and gives only a brief foundation here.

questions.question: What does this choice suggest about the passage’s purpose at this point?
questions.answer: It suggests the goal here is to summarize and introduce, not to fully expand every detail.

questions.question: What stopped the writing of the remaining mysteries?
questions.answer: Two serious barriers, one outward and one inward, prevented it.

questions.question: In simple words, what is the “Third Truth” about in this passage?
questions.answer: It is about understanding Allah’s oneness through His unlimited power, which makes all creation equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What does the passage call this truth besides a truth of unity?
questions.answer: It also calls it a useful wisdom, a great key, a difficult riddle, and a major foundation of faith.

questions.question: Why are so many grand descriptions used for this truth?
questions.answer: To show that it is extremely important, deep, and helpful for belief.

questions.question: What does the passage say becomes opened by explaining this truth?
questions.answer: A hidden lock of the Qur’an is opened.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to philosophy in front of this mystery?
questions.answer: Philosophy is left powerless before it.

questions.question: What book is praised for solving this matter?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How does the passage support the claim that this matter has been solved?
questions.answer: It says the matter was proven with strong and definite arguments in specific parts of that work.

questions.question: What level of certainty is given for those arguments?
questions.answer: They are said to be certain in a very clear and undeniable way.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention several sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To show where readers can find fuller proofs and discussions of this matter.

questions.question: What does the writer still want to provide in this passage?
questions.answer: A short explanation of the basic proofs and an indication of thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: Why is the number thirteen important here?
questions.answer: Because the writer planned to arrange the explanation into thirteen parts.

questions.question: What happened after the first two parts were written?
questions.answer: The remaining parts were left unfinished because of two difficult obstacles.

questions.question: What central belief is being strengthened in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s unity and perfect power.

questions.question: What special mystery about creation is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: That for Allah, creating something vast and creating something tiny are the same in ease.

questions.question: Why would this idea strengthen a believer’s faith?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s power has no limits and is not weakened by the size or number of things.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation makes possible for a person to know?
questions.answer: It makes it possible to know a very hidden secret about the creation of beings.

questions.question: What is one way the passage shows the greatness of this truth?
questions.answer: It says this truth is among the most important bases of Islam and faith.

questions.question: What response does the writer show after speaking about the solution to this mystery?
questions.answer: The writer responds with abundant praise and thanks to Allah.

questions.question: Which work is presented as the means by which this mystery was clarified?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How strong are the proofs said to be in that work?
questions.answer: They are described as firm, clear, and decisive.

questions.question: What does the writer choose not to do fully in this passage?
questions.answer: The writer does not give the complete detailed proof here.

questions.question: What does the writer choose to do instead?
questions.answer: The writer gives a short presentation of the foundations and points toward thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What had already been completed from that plan?
questions.answer: The first and second mysteries.

questions.question: What prevented the rest from being finished?
questions.answer: Two powerful difficulties, one physical and one non-physical.

questions.question: What does the passage try to prove about Allah’s relationship to creation?
questions.answer: It tries to prove that Allah alone can create all things, and that nothing is too great or too small for Him.

questions.question: What idea about “great” and “small” is stressed in the passage?
questions.answer: It stresses that both are equal before Allah’s power.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is this truth valuable for Muslims?
questions.answer: Because it supports tawhid and serves as a deep basis for Islamic belief.

questions.question: What two big areas are connected by this explanation?
questions.answer: It connects understanding the Qur’an with understanding the creation of beings.

questions.question: How is human philosophy shown in comparison with this mystery?
questions.answer: It is shown as too weak to master or solve it by itself.

questions.question: What emotional tone appears when the passage speaks about the solving of this mystery?
questions.answer: A tone of gratitude, praise, and relief appears.

questions.question: What source is credited with solving and proving the mystery?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is credited.

questions.question: Does the passage present the proof as doubtful or settled?
questions.answer: It presents it as settled and strongly established.

questions.question: Why are other parts of the Risale-i Nur mentioned?
questions.answer: Because the fuller treatment of the matter is left to those sections.

questions.question: What does the writer still hope to do in this passage?
questions.answer: The writer hopes to briefly lay out the main bases of the explanation.

questions.question: What picture is used to describe the thirteen mysteries?
questions.answer: They are pictured as steps or like an outline of topics.

questions.question: What interrupted the completion of all thirteen?
questions.answer: Two powerful obstacles interrupted the work.

questions.question: What is the key mystery discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: The key mystery is that Allah’s power makes the largest universal thing and the smallest particular thing equal in ease.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this mystery as something very great?
questions.answer: Because it is tied to Divine unity, faith, and the understanding of creation and the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage say this explanation unlocks?
questions.answer: It unlocks a hidden wisdom connected to the Qur’an.

questions.question: What hidden area of knowledge becomes clearer through this?
questions.answer: The secret of how created beings come into existence becomes clearer.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the limits of human reason alone?
questions.answer: It suggests that reason by itself cannot fully reach this deep matter.

questions.question: What act of worship appears in the middle of the passage?
questions.answer: Thanking and praising Allah.

questions.question: What is said to have accomplished the explanation and proof of this mystery?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is said to have done so.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the strength of its arguments?
questions.answer: It describes them as decisive and certain.

questions.question: Why does the writer send readers to other sections instead of explaining everything here?
questions.answer: Because those sections already treat the matter in detail, while this place is for a brief presentation.

questions.question: What did the writer plan to include after the brief foundations?
questions.answer: The writer planned to mention thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: How much of that plan was actually completed?
questions.answer: Only the first two mysteries were written.

questions.question: What caused the rest to remain unfinished?
questions.answer: Two major obstacles, one material and one immaterial, caused the writer to stop.
